newsitem.title: USA: Commonwealth to send mission to Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth to send mission to Nigeria.

text.p: Commonwealth ministers on Sunday backed away from possible conflict with Nigeria, abandoning talk of sanctions for the time being and agreeing to send a fact-finding mission to the oil-rich African state.

The ministers softened their position on the fact-finding mission by abandoning an earlier insistence that Nigeria should guarantee Commonwealth officials access to opposition groups and human rights campaigners.
The eight-nation Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) agreed a set of sanctions in April but suspended them until September to give Nigeria more chance for dialogue.

"Since we have decided to go to Nigeria the measures we approved will not be implemented," Zimbabwean Foreign Minister Stan Mudenge told reporters after CMAG held two days of talks on how to push Nigeria back onto the road to democracy.

The Commonwealth suspended Nigeria last November after it executed author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other human rights activists. It made clear the suspension would stay until CMAG was able to fully investigate human rights in Nigeria.

Last month CMAG scrapped a fact-finding mission when Abuja denied access to opposition groups. Mudenge said the ministers now "hoped" the military government of General Sani Abacha would let them speak to whoever they wanted.
